purpose: Persistent individual-level agent model for every citizen in LYRA. No citizen is represented only as a demographic average.

personality.rule: Values and personality are persistent but not perfectly consistent. Situational pressure can override traits.

knowledgeAndBelief.knownFacts: Facts personally observed or reliably transmitted.
knowledgeAndBelief.beliefs: Claims believed with confidence 0-1, including false beliefs.
knowledgeAndBelief.rumors: Unverified claims with source and transmission history.

goals.rule: Goals are derived from age, household, occupation, values and current constraints; they can change after major events.

relationships.rule: Relationships are directional. A may trust B more than B trusts A.

civicBehavior.rule: These are not fixed political ideology labels. Policy reaction is recomputed from lived effects and relationships.

memory.longTerm: Sparse durable memories with emotional weight.
memory.recent: Last important events affecting current decisions.
memory.decayRule: Low-salience facts decay or distort; emotionally intense memories persist.

steps: evaluate effects on household and protected goals
apply personality, stress and social pressure
choose action from feasible actions, not ideal actions

uniquenessConstraints: No two citizens may share the same complete personality/value vector.
No citizen is generated as a stereotype of their country's objective function.
Country-level culture changes priors only; individual variance must dominate.
At least 15% of adults in every country should strongly disagree with the current governing tendency on one major value dimension.
At least 10% of citizens should have internally conflicting high values that create recurring tradeoffs.
Traits must correlate plausibly with age, occupation, household role and life history rather than being independently random.
